column3: I predict one of the surprises, to some people anyway, is going to be that autonomous vehicles don't clog city streets.
If there is a task with enough value to automate, a specialized robot will win that market.
I would bet against the imminent commodification of autonomous vehicle technology.
Effectively every single H100 in existence now will be e-waste in 5 years or less.
Selling the output of a LLM is going to an incredibly cut-throat and low-margin business.
I think SWE headcounts will reduce over time.
as model capabilities plateau (I'm not an accelerationist) the harnesses and products around them will start to specialize.
The 128 GB Mac Studio is no longer sold and when they bring it back I predict it will be more expensive.
I think it will split between TSMC (sold out forever) and Samsung/Intel (please please be our customer).
I would bet that AIs will master taste and human psychology before they'll cure cancer.
in two years time Waymo will probably be available to the majority of the US population.
We might have 600MW of SMR's within a decade, but we're highly unlikely to have 6GW.
I'll believe in three years we'll be able to run ~30B models on the best phones.
in the end I suspect efficiency will be the winning feature.
If I could bet on this, I would bet everything I could on "skill with LLMs" being the high order bit of being an effective software developer 5 years from now.
They've all avoided loading up their LLMs with ads to this point. That is going to change dramatically over the next 2-3 years.
Half of PayPal's business goes away over the coming decade.
these computing price increases will be what finally makes certain ML startups un-economical.
I think the Internet will, sometime in the near future, just get shut down.
I won’t be surprised if my kid looks back on Anthropic and OpenAI the way we look back on Sun and Netscape.
It seems very very unlikely that an Opus 5 matching local model that runs on a 5070 will be released within the next 5 years.
I think Anthropic and OpenAI's margins will erode some over time.
The cuts will have arrived by 2030, but the bill will be old news.
